### Discussed in #9960 [...] After doing more testing, i've noticed two things:

First thing; i was quantizing models with --leave-output-tensor, which made my models run very slow under Linux too. That was a side-effect of my investigation, and i'm leaving that in case somebody else has this issue :)

Second thing, closely related to the issue: some models work just fine.  
 In my first test, i was checking Qwen2.5 14B finetune, quantized to Q6\_K. This model behaves the same on Windows whether i leave the output tensor as-is, or not, in terms of memory allocation. Not leaving output tensor increases performance a small bit, but it's not very noticeable due to memory constraints.

HOWEVER, LLaMA 3.2 3B quantized to Q8\_0 works just fine, and is loaded to dedicated GPU memory!  
 What's going on here?

results.title: Releases · ggml-org/Llama-Windows · GitHub
results.content:
A dead llama server is detected again: a failing `GET /models` is confirmed against `/health`, so the app reports "the server stopped responding" instead of showing a phantom "running" forever (#115).
 Fixed a rare cross-thread race on the shared settings collections that could wedge the background model watcher (#119).
 Server reads and writes stay outside the MSIX virtualization sandbox, fixing settings/models that could split across real and virtual paths (#108, fixes #107).
 Removing a managed installation deletes only Llama's own files from the shared install directory (#95).
 Correct architecture detection on ARM64 machines (#101).
 Providers without a bundled brand mark show the org's Hub avatar instead of an empty tile (#112). [...] ## Chat overlay confinement (#86)

The overlay is a borderless window with no address bar, so anything it renders carries the app's visual authority. The embedded WebUI can now only ever display pages  
 from your local llama server: top-level and iframe navigations off the server's origin are cancelled, new windows go to the system browser (plain http/https only),  
 and DevTools are disabled in release builds.

## Model-id and input validation (#82)

Model ids come from remote data and were previously trusted too far: they're now validated before being used as cache paths (closing a path-traversal that could probe  
 files outside the cache) and JSON-escaped in every request body. The copyable sample curl command is now safely serialized and shell-quoted.

## Supply chain (#87) [...] update dependencies to latest version by @mfuntowicz in #92
 fix(app): remove only Llama's files from the shared install dir by @mfuntowicz in #95
 Add ability to share images and text to the llama server by @mfuntowicz in #98
 Add llama:// protocol deep links (chat prompt, model load) by @mfuntowicz in #99
 Fix/arch detection by @mfuntowicz in #101
 misc: update publisher for the windows store by @mfuntowicz in #102
 Add speculative decoding support by @mfuntowicz in #105
 Enroll local model folders for discovery by @mfuntowicz in #106
 fix(server): keep every server-read path out of the MSIX virtualization sandbox by @mfuntowicz in #108
 Put the server API key behind the same door as the HF token by @mfuntowicz in #109
